heuristics: H1 (random-function model): with published pseudorandom constants c_j = sha512(...) mod r, walker states collide at the parallel-rho birthday rate t^2/(2(r-1)), distinguished-point counts are Binomial(t, 2^-32), and cycle entries occur at the self-pair birthday scale t^2/(2Kr) = 6.329e-01 with total waste <= t^2/(6K^2 r) = 5.935e-67 of the budget, subtracted in the success model (cycles containing a distinguished point are detected at the first DP revisit and reseeded; cycles containing none waste at most the remaining budget, bounded over the un-terminated budget). No rescaling of the scalar confines the step set: Part A measures every M <= 2^12 (narrowest window 0.0000 of r, and the same check detects the rejected v6 constants at 6.06e-11) and the counting heuristic 32*W^31/r^30 puts expected confiners of width <= 2^240 below 2^{heur_exp:.0f}. The toy measures 1.052 of the birthday ideal (two-sigma 0.129).

Efficiency floor 0.75: ~29% below the toy-measured ratio 1.052, and consistent with Teske's measured r-adding-walk collision factors (at most ~1.1x the random-walk ideal for r >= 16); the floor covers a production walk 33% slower than that worst measured factor; the claimed success is computed at this floor (0.4066249786 >= 0.39) and does not depend on the measurement beyond the floor's support.
limitations: Analytic construction; no production-size execution is claimed or possible.
Single-shot randomized attack at the 0.39 threshold (modeled success 0.4066 at the 0.75 efficiency floor).
The distinguished-point table is a hard 2^98-slot allocation (2^105 bytes); overflow aborts with probability <= exp(-2^95.9) under H1, subtracted.

Standard cryptanalysis (parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points and pseudorandom published constants); the confinement analysis (executed rescaling certificate plus counting bound) and the itemized full-coverage ledger are the contribution under this cost model.
